concept_html:
Everything in Fabric sits in one hierarchy. Learn it first, because cost, access and deployment all follow it.

  • Tenant. Your organisation's Microsoft Entra ID tenant. Tenant settings, set by Fabric administrators, apply to everything below.
  • Capacity. A pool of compute you buy. Every Fabric workload, from Spark to Power BI, draws from the capacity its workspace is assigned to.
  • Workspace. A container where a team creates and shares items. Access is granted per workspace, through roles (lesson C1-L3).
  • Item. A lakehouse, warehouse, notebook, pipeline, semantic model, report, eventhouse and so on. Items hold or process the data.

Capacities come as SKUs. F SKUs are the recommended Fabric capacities. The number is the compute in capacity units (CUs): an F2 has 2 CUs, an F64 has 64, up to F2048. A trial capacity has 64 CUs. Microsoft 365 P SKUs also run Fabric if Fabric is enabled on them.

Size affects licensing, not only speed. On F64 or larger (or a P capacity), users with a free Fabric license can view Power BI content. On smaller F SKUs, each viewer needs a Pro, Premium Per User or individual trial licence.

Pausing a capacity stops compute billing while it is paused. It is not free of consequences: when you pause, any smoothed and overage usage still owed is added to your Azure bill at once, and items on that capacity stop working until you resume.

Two practical rules follow from the hierarchy:

  • Put dev, test and production in separate workspaces, and assign production to a capacity that experiments cannot exhaust.
  • Before you design anything, find out which capacity SKU you have. It decides what users need to pay for and how much work runs at once.

Facts in this lesson come from Microsoft Learn's licensing and capacity pages, checked September 2026.

"""Capacity-unit hours for running an F SKU capacity.
sku: F SKU name such as "F64".

if sku not in F_SKUS:
raise ValueError(f"unknown F SKU: {sku!r}")
raise ValueError("hours must not be negative")
return float(F_SKUS[sku] * hours)

title: Tenant, capacity, workspace and item
why_html: A team built a Power BI report for 300 frontline managers on an F32 capacity, assuming that managers with free licences could view it, as they had on the old Premium P1. Launch day produced 300 "You need a license" messages. The fix was either 300 Pro licences or a move to F64. Neither was in the budget, and the launch slipped a quarter.
